questions.stem: Which masking approach does Data Redaction work most like?
questions.explanation: Data Redaction does not work like SDM; it works pretty much like DDM, blacking out data on the fly.

questions.stem: What does Data Redaction do to data?
options: Copies it to a masked dataset for developers
Blacks it out on the fly, so the result may not even make sense to the user
Stores it in a Token Vault
Swaps it with values from other records
questions.explanation: Data Redaction blacks out the data on the fly, and the redacted output may or may not make sense to the users seeing it.

questions.stem: What are the four types of Data Redaction?
questions.explanation: The four types of Data Redaction are Random, RedExp, Partial and Full.

questions.stem: What is masked in the RedExp type of Data Redaction?
questions.explanation: In RedExp redaction, expressions are masked.

questions.stem: A card transaction message showing all digits as stars except the last few is an example of which type of Data Redaction?
questions.explanation: The stars on a card number are redacted values where only some of the data is masked, which is Partial redaction.

questions.stem: What happens in Full Data Redaction?
options: Some of the data is masked
Nothing is masked but access is logged
questions.explanation: In Full redaction everything is masked, whereas Partial masks only some of the data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the types of Data Redaction?
questions.explanation: The four types are Random, RedExp, Partial and Full; Static is not one of them, and redaction works on the fly rather than statically.

questions.stem: How is data masked in the Random type of Data Redaction?
options: Only for the last few characters
questions.explanation: In Random redaction the data is masked randomly.

questions.stem: What is true of the output of Data Redaction as seen by users?
options: It is reversible by the user
It is permanently written back to the datastore
It always preserves the original meaning
It may or may not even make sense to the users using it
questions.explanation: Redaction blacks out data on the fly, and the result may or may not make sense to the users using it.

questions.stem: Which statement about Data Redaction is correct?
options: It creates a permanent masked copy like SDM
It is identical to Data Masking
It works on the fly, like DDM, rather than like SDM
It stores mappings in a Token Vault
It only applies to structured data
questions.explanation: Data Redaction is confused with data masking, but it does not work like SDM; it works pretty much like DDM, on the fly.
